svg.title: E1: a current match, explained on demand
svg.desc: Standalone editable SVG for the E1 match explanation. Numbered flow follows MatchExplanationService.explain. Supporting Mermaid diagrams: docs/diagrams/E1.md.

g.text: E1: a current match, explained on demand
Scores and ranks remain deterministic. Freshness is checked before optional cache, quota or provider work.
Only the digest reaches the UI.
state do not change the score ID.
clear text and abort old request.
Same Java scoring; active/non-self candidate contract.
Core validation, authorization and eligibility errors propagate.
Stop before optional work, including when AI is off.
Use the current deterministic MatchExplainer text.
4 Reduce evidence and derive its cache key
Rounded semantic key is separate from the exact card ID.
5 Look up and revalidate cached text
ExplanationCache.find(hash); current validator on every hit.
Valid hit → AI. Invalid hit or read failure → STANDARD.
Only a cache miss continues; no quota spent on a hit/error.
6 Build the prompt from plain-word evidence
ExplanationPromptBuilder fills prompt v5 via PromptTemplate.
ExplanationVocabulary: plain words and weights, no code names.
The student ID is kept for the allowance; Gemini never sees it.
7 Call Gemini within E1’s quota, validate, cache
GeminiClient, which spends its AiQuota before calling.
Over quota, 429 pause, failure or rejected output → STANDARD.
Validated output → AI, even if cache.save() fails.
Provider key stays on the backend.
Unique evidence hash; no student FK.
ONE DTO SHAPE; THREE CLEAR OUTCOMES
The UI labels it and asks the student to check
the score breakdown. No score or rank changes.
cache read failure or configuration not ready.
A cache write failure still returns valid AI text.
Core matching errors retain their contract.
These errors are not hidden by AI fallback.
The orchestration holds no database transaction across the external call. Output checks are bounded: they reject known unsafe patterns, not every inaccurate sentence.
